This seems similar in principle to a variety of other issues, such as #10101, #9479, #10277. 

Given the https://llmsmetatags.org/ exists, what benefit do we gain by incorporating this into the HTML specification? For example https://schema.org/ exists, is widely used, and is not incorporated into the HTML specification.

Why not `<link rel="llms-website" href="https://ai.example.com">`? Links provide more flexibility than meta tags in terms of additional context (encoding, content type), and can be embeded in sitemap.xml and http headers.

> This seems similar in principle to a variety of other issues, such as [#10101](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10101), [#9479](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9479), [#10277](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10277).
> 
> Given the https://llmsmetatags.org/ exists, what benefit do we gain by incorporating this into the HTML specification? For example https://schema.org/ exists, is widely used, and is not incorporated into the HTML specification.

Issue [#10277](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10277) has a similar purpose. The tag `ai:task` could be incorporated on LLMs Meta Tags Standard.

Incorporating LLMs into HTML could standardize tag implementation across systems, similar to what OpenGraph achieves.

> Why not `<link rel="llms-website" href="https://ai.example.com">`? Links provide more flexibility than meta tags in terms of additional context (encoding, content type), and can be embeded in sitemap.xml and http headers.

It is a good suggestion that can be incorporated into the standard, for this specific tag.

> Incorporating LLMs into HTML could standardize tag implementation across systems, similar to what OpenGraph achieves.

OpenGraph is not part of the HTML specification. It is specified at https://ogp.me/ instead. So I think the question remains.

> > Incorporating LLMs into HTML could standardize tag implementation across systems, similar to what OpenGraph achieves.
> 
> OpenGraph is not part of the HTML specification. It is specified at https://ogp.me/ instead. So I think the question remains.

Allright. So in this case we can close this propose.
Thanks for the advice.

@rafaelp : I like this idea but I see this is closed, can you suggest on the best way to make the llms.txt file auto discoverable to AI Agents ? As of now, I see that they are not pretrained to lookup at this file unlike search engines to look at sitemap files.

*Figure 1: I Am Bonkers. Who Let This Halfway Homeless Totally **Phoneless
Nutcase Near a Computer Anyway?*

Forgive me the garish composition. I think some expression really does
require human gesture, whether recorded in a pen stroke or performed in a
pit ... and the most invidious spade must be named such in neon. Let’s go
back in time a bit ... The disingenuous opengraph pseudostandard was an
exploitative gambit that sought to make facebook’s platform-eating,
rent-seeking by injecting itself as a mediator between publisher and reader
whose demands could not be ignored in practice (facebook was still
ascendent), and tho it ultimately failed at that fer a few cool reasons and
fb never got anywhere close to real viable EEE, it had a second purpose
that it did succeed at: conscript, and in turn, effectively mandate, that
authors *work for them for free.* and that’s just what happened, gleefully,
nearly every last fool among us shruggin’ and complying without thinking
about the bigger picture or a longer now or interrogating the consequences
of the “design” “decisions” or where power was located and how governance
work and who the stakeholders were and what the alternatives might have
been and so on, self included. things did mostly work out many years later
— twitter deserves some credit fer the initially defanging — first due to
an erosion and eventually an ossification and now we’re left with something
that sucks but isn’t actively anti-web, cool. Anyway, though such
“solutions” — lol! *lol!* LOL! y’all CAN laugh at the unclothed would-be
emperors, ya know — especially those out on their appointed rounds in doin’
silly clown cars drive-by discourse drop-offs rife with disguised demands
machine manufactured by the wizard of oz corps. and yes i know they
probably are True Believers; forgive ’em father, fer they’*re ridiculous
hacks* — *cough* though such “solutions” as were offered here like so
many *urgent
(oh so urgent! now and forever! lol) *rat corpses left upon one’s doorstep
ostensibly needed so we solve the problems of tomorrow that they’re taking
care of creating today ... *for them,* lol. although facebook demonstrated
plenty of open contempt towards ... well, basically everybody (users,
authors, developers, and the “faith economy” at the heart of the  web
standards ecosystem and its healthy stewardship with *their *socially
engineered trojan horse fer extracting free labor that was based in large
part on bogus meta elements, it’s positively angelic next to *(arms waving
around in the suffocating miasma of the death cultists)* this fetid volley.
because of the underlying perversity of the incentives and the level of
indirection and collective collaborative dishonesty in play, i do not see
any clear paths out of the overall morass that this is just one rank and
already clipped would-be tendril of that does not involve REALLY SPEAKING,
which looks like, among other things, this. Surely I could do far better
lol, and most likely it will be correctly identified, whether by real user
or ab—*er *by *“*automation,” i mean, as a violation of not only one or
another maritime laws but also good taste itself: aight lol, fair enuf, and
no hard feelings or anything to whoever *does *delete it, if someone does,
and much love to any humans who’ve read it; a human was here :)

no doubt i made mostly errors above — no need to refute ’em fer my sake,
but feel free fer others; i dunt come around here often these days.
hopefully i’ve made yr day more interesting.

     archfool cursed to believe in the world wide web despite everything,
     *billy mtv *(darien in specland)
